 import seaborn as sns
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import pandas as pd

    'Year': [2015, 2015, 2015, 2016, 2016, 2016, 2017, 2017, 2017,
             2018, 2018, 2018, 2019, 2019, 2019, 2020, 2020, 2020,
             2021, 2021, 2021, 2022, 2022, 2022, 2023, 2023, 2023,
             2024, 2024, 2024],
    'Education Sector': ['K-12', 'Higher Education', 'Vocational'] * 10,
    'Budget Allocation (%)': [
        33.0, 20.5, 11.0, 34.2, 21.0, 11.3, 34.5, 21.5, 11.7,
        35.2, 22.0, 12.0, 36.1, 22.3, 12.2, 36.8, 22.5, 12.3,

        38.5, 23.5, 12.7
    ],
    'R&D Spending (Billion USD)': [
        40.2, 60.3, 20.0, 41.9, 61.9, 22.0, 44.0, 63.6, 24.5,
        46.1, 65.3, 27.0, 48.3, 67.2, 29.5, 50.1, 68.6, 31.5,
        52.2, 70.1, 34.4, 53.4, 71.4, 35.5, 55.0, 72.8, 37.2,
        56.7, 74.2, 39.1
    ],
    'Student Enrollment Growth (%)': [
        0.5, 0.7, 0.3, 0.8, 0.6, 0.4, 1.0, 0.9, 0.5,
        1.2, 1.1, 0.6, 1.3, 1.2, 0.7, 1.4, 1.0, 0.8,
        1.1, 0.8, 0.6, 1.0, 0.7, 0.5, 0.8, 0.6, 0.4,
        0.6, 0.5, 0.3
    ]
}

df = pd.DataFrame(data)

plt.figure(figsize=(12, 7))
sns.boxplot(
    data=df[df['Education Sector'] != 'Vocational'],
    x='Education Sector',
    y='Budget Allocation (%)',
    hue='Education Sector',
    palette=['#4E79A7', '#F28E2B', '#E15759']
)
plt.title('Distribution of Education Budget Allocation by Sector (2015-2024)', fontsize=14, pad=20)
plt.xlabel('Education Sector', fontsize=12)
plt.ylabel('Budget Allocation (%)', fontsize=12)
plt.grid(axis='y', linestyle='--', alpha=0.7)
plt.tight_layout()
plt.savefig('output.png')

SUMMARY
 This image is a violin plot depicting the distribution of education budget allocation by sector from 2015 to 2024. The chart presents three distinct education sectors: K-12, Higher Education, and Vocational, each represented by a differently colored violin shape. The K-12 sector is shown in a deep blue shade, Higher Education in a warm orange tone, and Vocational in a rich red hue.

The vertical axis, labeled "Budget Allocation (%)", measures the percentage of the total education budget allocated to each sector, ranging from 10% to 35%. The horizontal axis categorizes the data into the three education sectors. Each violin plot displays the density of budget allocations over the given period, with wider sections indicating a greater concentration of data points at those values. Inside each violin, horizontal lines mark the quartiles, providing a sense of data distribution and central tendency.

For the K-12 sector, the budget allocation predominantly ranges between approximately 33% and 38.5%, with the thickest part of the violin around 35% to 37%, indicating the most common allocation percentages. The Higher Education sector’s budget allocation spans from about 20.5% to 23.5%, with a concentration around 22% to 23%. The Vocational sector shows a narrower range of budget allocations, roughly between 11% and 12.7%, with the majority clustering around 12% to 12.5%. This visualization effectively highlights the differences in budget allocation distribution among the three education sectors over the specified timeframe.

from pathlib import Path
p = Path("chart.py")
script = p.read_text()
script = script.replace("sns.boxplot(", "sns.violinplot(")
script = script.replace("data=df[df['Education Sector'] != 'Vocational'],", "data=df,\n    inner='quartile',\n    cut=0,")
p.write_text(script)
exec(compile(script, "chart.py", "exec"))
ax = plt.gca()
print("Plot type:", len(ax.collections), "collections")
print("Sectors:", [t.get_text() for t in ax.get_xticklabels()])
print("Y limits:", ax.get_ylim())
print("Title:", ax.get_title())
print("Axis labels:", ax.get_xlabel(), "/", ax.get_ylabel())
print("Quartile line count:", len(ax.lines))
table = pd.read_csv("table.csv")
pd.testing.assert_frame_equal(
    df[table.columns].sort_values(list(table.columns)).reset_index(drop=True),
    table.sort_values(list(table.columns)).reset_index(drop=True)
)
print("Plotted data match table.csv.")
